references.text: Describes the ancient custom in Israel where one removed a sandal and gave it to the other party to confirm a transaction or right of redemption, serving as background for the ritual in Deuteronomy
Isaiah mentions being spat upon as part of humiliation and disgrace, reflecting the act of spitting in someone's face as a sign of contempt
The Lord notes that if a father had spit in his daughter's face, she would have been shamed for seven days, showing spitting as a sign of shame and rejection
The immediate context explaining the levirate marriage law and the duty to build up one's brother's house
The continuation describing the consequence of the ritual - the man's family shall be called 'the house of the unsandaled' in Israel
The entire passage in Ruth tells how Boaz redeemed Ruth and took over the right of redemption at the city gate before the elders, with the sandal ritual as confirmation
